summary: Large contact-center SaaS evaluating Redwood for agent assist + RAG over heterogeneous support KBs. Primary goals: evidence-backed responses (snippet citations), freshness SLA for docs, multi-source retrieval (Zendesk + Confluence + product repos), and predictable performance during marketing/customer spikes.
notes: Head of Support (A. Martinez): 'We need answers we can cite back to customers — show me the source.'
Interested in structured tool-calling for ticket actions (create/update ticket, escalate, run playbooks) — needs function-calling + idempotency guarantees.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, corporate KMS, audit trails, and EU data residency for some customers.
Primary integration stack: Zendesk (tickets), Confluence (KB), GitHub (product docs), internal SQL store (legacy KB). Want connectors or incremental ingestion.
Cost sensitivity: mid-high — favor predictable reserved capacity but want Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization.
Model preference: instruction-tuned open models acceptable, but must support token-level cost breakdown and fallback policies. Need function-calling and streaming responses for agent desktop UX.
Quote from trial call: 'We can't have the system hallucinate — citations per snippet are non-negotiable.'
Asked for sample RAG flow that returns 3 ranked citations with context window and confidence score.
Prefers canary rollouts for any model change; wants eval-triggered rollback on quality regressions tied to a set of 2k test prompts.
CE/Infra asks: network egress policy, VPC peering diagram, and whether private control plane supports on-prem connectors.
Mentioned prior experiences: slow spikes during product launches caused 30-45s timeouts on existing home-grown solution — reliability is a top KPI.
Reference artifacts: security FAQ in Drive, Zendesk export sample shared in Gmail thread.
Wants token-level cost dashboard for routing decisions (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

technical_requirements: RAG must return top-3 citations with source id, snippet offsets, and freshness timestamp.
Support multi-source retrieval: Zendesk exports, Confluence pages, GitHub docs, SQL dump. Need incremental ingestion and delta syncs.
Freshness SLA: <24h for KB updates; channel-specific TTLs (urgent KBs <1h).
Hybrid retrieval: lexical + dense; prefer vector DB that supports semantic + metadata filtering (product version, region, language).
Chunking strategy: preserve paragraph-level context, but include overlap to keep provenance spans intact.
Citation policy: prefer exact-snippet citation and confidence score; for any answer shown to customers require at least one primary-source citation.
Tool-calling: atomic ticket actions via function-calls; idempotency and audit trail required.
Latency/throughput targets: 95th pct latency for agent-assist <250ms (in-region), peak concurrency 100 agents, peak QPS 200. Batch ticket summarization acceptable up to 5s per job but prefer <2s.
Reliability: graceful degradation to cached answers and smaller quantized model on overload; automatic fallback routing across regions and model tiers.
Observability: per-route tracing, token-level cost breakdown, quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
Compliance: EU data residency for EU customers, HSM/KMS support for keys, full audit logs retention 1 year (with option to extend).
poc_plan: Week 1-2: connector implementation (Zendesk + Confluence) + baseline ingestion and vector index build.
Week 3: retrieval strategy experiments (dot-product vs. hybrid) + citation formatting and snippet anchoring.
Week 4-5: agent desktop integration (tool-calls), end-to-end agent assist flows, ticket summarization pipeline.
Week 6: spike simulation (synthetic traffic), SLA verification, quality regression tests vs 2k eval set.
Success criteria: 95th pct latency <250ms for agent-assist, citation accuracy >90% on curated test set, stable performance under 2x expected peak.
Deliverables: SOW, infra diagram, perf report, security attestation snippet, and recommended Optimize settings (batching/quantization).
